title: French students and unions stage nationwide protests over schools and living costs
seoTitle: Paris nationwide protests over living costs

tea.why: Protesters are angry about poor school conditions, rising fuel prices, and the cost of living under President Emmanuel Macron's leadership.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand more teachers, better learning conditions in schools, lower fuel costs, and policy changes.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu reported that 1,200 people were detained nationwide following widespread unrest.

summary: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France, including Paris, in demonstrations addressing teaching conditions, rising fuel prices, and the overall cost of living. Organised in part by students, school groups, and various leftist unions, the demonstrations involved peaceful marches alongside clashes, property damage, and arson in several cities, such as the torching of the Limoges City Hall and attacks on public offices. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu blamed radical left groups for stoking violence from the beginning, while police deployed tear gas and water cannons in the capital. Government officials reported over a thousand arrests nationwide, numerous injured police officers, and severe property destruction, prompting President Emmanuel Macron to warn that vandals would be prosecuted.
response: According to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, police responded to escalating violence and arson with tear gas and water cannons, and arrested 1,200 people nationwide. President Emmanuel Macron warned that all vandals and looters would be prosecuted and punished.

crowd.text: An estimated 550,000 people took part in demonstrations across France

updates.text: Dozens of arrests occurred in Paris as nationwide demonstrations commenced over schools and the cost of living.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that 550,000 protesters participated across the country, with 110,000 in Paris.
Clashes and arson broke out in multiple cities, destroying historic buildings like the Limoges City Hall and tourist offices.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu updated the nationwide detention toll to 1,200 individuals amid escalating unrest.
